text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Relations between Singapore and United States are on solid footing, with two countries enjoying close ties strategically and politically, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright says.

- Youths who commit offences may be slapped with court order to perform community service, or be sentenced to weekend detention in rehabilitation centre, under move to give courts wider range of options in dealing with juvenile offenders.
- ASEAN's peace mission to Cambodia will resume, probably within days, after co-premier Hun Sen confirmes he welcomes ASEAN role to help restore political stability in his country.
- Creative Technology chief Sim Wong Hoo finds it "amusing" analysts regard rival Venture Manufacturing's new NovaStation software as possible threat to Creative's SoundBlaster products.

- Creative turns in record full-year earnings of Singapore $245.5 million but sterling results fail to spur local share price further because of profit taking and overnight loss on Nasdaq, where soundcard maker is also listed.
- All new buildings in Marina South's new downtown will be required to have pedestrian links -- either underground or on second storey -- to provide direct access to public transport.

- Property market "becoming more sickly by the day" and prices of private houses and condominiums are heading for collapse, developers told Minister of National Development in recent letter of appeal.
- White House and congressional Republicans, after seven months of haggling, reach "historic agreement" to balance federal spending by 2002 that includes biggest US tax cuts in 16 years.
- Khoo Teck Puat's Central Properties announces 27.3 percent rise in group after-tax profit to S$13.28 million at half-time.
- Sin Soon Huat, just upgraded to main board from Sesdaq, is gunning for region in big way.
- DBS Land, which recently bought 19 percent stake in Parkway for S$390 million, rumoured to be close to deal for another major block of shares in company.
- Hongkong-listed China Strategic Holdings raising about S$86 million through private placement of 132 million new shares.
